---
description: "Use when creating, modifying, or formatting Markdown documentation across the repository."
applyTo: "**/*.md"
---

# Documentation Guidelines

Markdown documentation lives in `docs/` and generated chart READMEs; it describes architecture, setup, and operations without duplicating manifests.

## Structure

| File/Directory                         | Responsibility                                                         |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md`      | Repository-wide instructions for `Copilot` and development guidelines. |
| `.github/instructions/`                | Domain-scoped instruction guides.                                      |
| `docs/README.md`                       | Central documentation index and architecture overview.                 |
| `docs/catalog/README.md`               | Catalog design standards, conventions, and application directory.      |
| `docs/catalog/<APPLICATION>.md`        | Architecture and setup documentation for a catalog application.        |
| `docs/clusters/README.md`              | Cluster management, GitOps topology, and descriptor conventions.       |
| `docs/clusters/<CLUSTER>.md`           | Cluster inventory, bootstrap procedure, networking, and runbooks.      |
| `kubernetes/catalog/<CHART>/README.md` | Chart reference generated by `helm-docs`; do not edit manually.        |

## Conventions

### Content

- Derive names, values, and commands directly from the code, manifests, and `Taskfile`; never invent values.
- Link to the owning manifest or documentation section instead of duplicating content.
- Explain why a procedure is necessary, not only the steps; mark irreversible or destructive steps with `> [!IMPORTANT]`.
- Write runbooks as ordered steps with clear validation commands.
- For chart reference documentation, update `values.yaml` comments and `Chart.yaml` metadata, then regenerate `README.md` using `helm-docs`.
- Structure each `docs/catalog/<APPLICATION>.md` as `Overview`, `Architecture`, `Dependencies`, `Configuration`, and `Setup`; in `Configuration`, list only key and mandatory parameters and link to `values.schema.json` instead of copying values.

### Formatting

- Write in English, present tense, active voice.
- Write headings in title case (e.g. `Bootstrap a Cluster`, `Deploy and Extend Applications`), including the document title and all section levels.
- Never wrap lines manually in Markdown: keep each paragraph, list item, and table row on one line, even beyond 120 characters (`markdownlint` `MD013` is disabled).
- Wrap identifiers, file names, environment variables, resource names, and commands in backticks.
- Write placeholders as `<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>` (e.g. `<CLUSTER>`, `<CHART>`, `<INSTANCE>`).
- Always specify a language tag on fenced code blocks (e.g. `sh`, `yaml`, `json`, `text`).
- Start every item of an ordered list with `1.`, and of a lettered list with `a.`.
- Use GitHub alerts for callouts: `> [!NOTE]`, `> [!IMPORTANT]`, `> [!WARNING]`, `> [!TIP]`.
- Use relative links and update anchors when renaming headings.
- Keep the table of contents of a document in sync with its headings.

## Validation

- Lint Markdown using `pre-commit run markdownlint-cli2 --all-files`.
- Verify formatting using `pre-commit run mdformat --all-files`.
- Verify that relative links and anchors resolve.

## Example

````markdown
# <DOCUMENT_TITLE>

- [<DOCUMENT_TITLE>](#document-title)
  - [<SECTION>](#section)

## <SECTION>

<PURPOSE_AND_CONTEXT>

```sh
helm dependency build kubernetes/catalog/<CHART>
helm upgrade --install <INSTANCE> kubernetes/catalog/<CHART>
```

> [!NOTE]
> <HINT>
````
